https://adi.dj/article/138990.standfirst: A boat with 305 people aboard sank off Obock on October 8–9. By October 11 the IOM and local authorities reported 139 dead, 84 missing and 82 survivors; searches continued.
body: The October 11 count of 139 dead, 84 missing and 82 survivors came from Djiboutian authorities and the International Organization for Migration. The boat reportedly carried 305 migrants and sank near Obock on the night of October 8–9.
AP's reporting explains why the count is provisional: some bodies buried by fellow migrants were not yet part of the official count. Most survivors were Ethiopian. Rescue and assistance continued.

The Eastern Route connects the Horn of Africa to Yemen and Gulf labor markets. Reports of vessel overloading and survivor experiences warrant further investigation; the exact cause has not been formally established.

https://www.dawn.com/news/2036352/federa.standfirst: President Zardari approved an emergency and governor's rule on October 11 in the opposition-led province. The federal government cites militancy; PTI disputes the takeover.
body: Dawn reported the October 11 proclamation under Pakistan's constitutional emergency and federal-intervention provisions. The federal government alleges the PTI administration did not cooperate sufficiently against militancy.
PTI argues the takeover violates democratic and provincial rights. Local Geo News reported the governor-led arrangement; Reuters independently reported the action and opposition response.
The key issue is not whether militancy exists, but whether the scope and duration of extraordinary federal powers are justified, reviewable and proportionate.

https://www.informador.mx/jalisco/huraca.standfirst: Jalisco issued red alerts and closed some activities as Simon passed close to shore. A late October 11 NHC advisory located it offshore with 105-knot winds; dangerous rain and surf continued.
body: Local El Informador reporting documented severe Jalisco alerts, disrupted activities and coastal precautions. The National Hurricane Center's advisory issued at 0300 UTC October 12 placed Simon offshore, with winds estimated near 105 knots.
The cyclone showed signs of weakening but rain, high surf and landslide risk remained serious. Terrain can amplify flooding far from the storm's center.
Forecasts should not be treated as observed landfall or confirmed damage. Latest Mexican civil-protection guidance remains essential for residents.

https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012002.standfirst: South Korea reported multiple October 12 launches near Pyongyang, with at least one missile traveling over 900 kilometers, after recent military tests on both sides.
body: Yonhap cited South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detecting missiles launched near Pyongyang on October 12. At least one was reported to have traveled more than 900 kilometers toward the East Sea.
The launch followed recent tests by both Koreas. That timing is consistent with signaling but does not prove North Korea's specific motive.
Reuters independently reported the event. Initial missile counts, technical characteristics and flight paths may be revised.

https://amazonasatual.com.br/governo-fed.standfirst: Smoke in Manaus prompted school closures; on October 11 Amazonas reported emergency recognition for 36 municipalities affected by fires.
body: Local Amazonas Atual reported emergency recognition for 36 municipalities on October 11 after forest fires and smoke affected the state. Manaus had suspended municipal classes on October 9.
Fine-particle pollution readings varied by monitoring location; some schools and universities shifted away from in-person activities. AP separately documented severe smoke and disruption.
Smoke sources include forest fires, other vegetation fires and waste burning. Attributing every local measurement to one fire would overstate the evidence.

https://www.unicef.org/reports/learning-.standfirst: A September UNICEF analysis found at least 171 million students experienced climate-related school interruptions in 2025 across 106 countries and territories.
body: UNICEF's September Learning Interrupted report compiled data from 106 countries and territories and estimated at least 171 million students faced weather-related schooling interruptions in 2025.

Disruptions included closed schools, lost instructional time and remote-learning shifts. They do not mean all students permanently dropped out. Three quarters of affected students lived in low- and lower-middle-income countries.
The minimum estimate depends on available country reporting. The report's potential lifetime earnings losses are modeled projections rather than observed future outcomes.

https://science.nasa.gov/missions/webb/w.standfirst: A MeerKAT radio flash was linked with Webb observations to a small galaxy at redshift 2.148, when the universe was roughly three billion years old.
body: MeerTRAP detected FRB 20240304B with South Africa's MeerKAT telescope. Webb then identified a faint, actively star-forming host galaxy at redshift 2.148.

The event dates to roughly three billion years after the Big Bang and extends the distance at which such bursts have been localized. The unexpectedly small host offers clues to the population of possible burst sources.
Radio waves passing through intergalactic matter carry useful information, but one record-setting burst does not establish the engine. Magnetars remain a hypothesis, not a settled conclusion.

https://aeon.co/essays/how-should-you-ch.standfirst: Irene McMullin argues that our projects, duties to particular people and obligations to society can make equally legitimate but incompatible demands.
body: Irene McMullin argues that many ethical dilemmas are not battles between goodness and temptation. People face competing legitimate demands that cannot always be satisfied together.

She distinguishes the first-person value of one's own projects, the second-person value of particular others and the third-person demands of a shared world. None can be translated without loss into the others.
The argument is that all three sources of value matter, while time and resources are limited. Thus ethical life requires a shifting balance developed over a whole life, not an algorithm for each act.

Consider a parent choosing a better-paying job that leaves less time for family and community. The conflict includes real goods on both sides; this is Morning Edition's illustration, not an example quoted from McMullin.
Her view draws on existentialism and virtue ethics and criticizes one-perspective versions of utilitarianism, Kantian duty and egoism, while recognizing that each captures something important.

A strong objection is that pluralism may justify selfishness and fail to direct urgent decisions. A possible reply, reconstructed from her essay, is that virtues, moral exemplars and patterns over time constrain judgment without making every choice simple.

https://publicdomainreview.org/essay/phi.standfirst: Florence Hazrat uses Philip Sidney's Arcadia to show how punctuation, interruption and digression shape literary voice.
body: Florence Hazrat's essay follows parentheses in Renaissance literary rhetoric and Philip Sidney's Arcadia. The mark can create a pause, a second voice, a correction or a digression.
The history shows that punctuation is not merely a grammatical convenience. It can change how readers experience thought and narrative rhythm.
This is a critical reading of literary form rather than a new empirical discovery. Other interpretations of Sidney remain possible.
